The instantons for (left) varying γ1 and (right) varying γ2 with dimensional salinities: (a),(f) SN; (b),(g) ST; (c),(h) SS; and (d),(i) SIP and (e),(j) the associated optimal freshwater forcings.

The instanton for an AMOC collapse from ϕON to ϕOFF and its reverse (the “anti-instanton”) are computed for the noise parameters (AN, AT, AS, AIP)T = (0.070, 0.752, −0.257, −0.565) which follow from the same calibration to the FAMOUS_B model (Wood et al. 2019). So, freshwater goes into boxes N and T, and as compensation, freshwater is extracted from boxes S and IP. This conserves the total salinity, and ϕON and ϕOFF do not change during the hosing process. Equation (12) is solved using the discussed augmented Lagrangian method, where explicit Euler is used for time integration with time step Δt = 0.05. The instantons ϕ(t) are terminated once ‖ϕ(T) − ϕend‖ < 10−5. For different values of 30 < T < 100, the trajectory of the instanton is just translated in time without any significant change in behavior. Moreover, the average times of a realization to transit from the ON basin (defined by q > 14 Sv) to the OFF basin (defined by q < −4.5 Sv) and vice versa level off for smaller noise levels (tested down to ϵ ∼ 0.035) at T = 17 and T = 32 for the collapse and recovery, respectively. Hence, T = 32 is sufficient to capture the relevant instanton behavior for both transition directions.
